links.reason: சொற்குன்றா in 1031 does return as சொற்குன்றான் in 1045, a real echo. But the note's letter-reading is not in the verse, and 'unequal risk' is the grader's inference; the offerings are not stated to need divine witnesses (நூலவையார் are the witnesses).

The Kural asks an open question about heaven versus the beloved's arms; 29 is a simile about Civakan having tasted greater bliss. No opposed ranking is stated in the Tamil, and 'rebuttal' needs a commentator's answer.
Both use தெய்வ மார்பகம் with the woman joining the lord, but the real relation is prophecy (407 'உரியள்') answered by 603 'மாதவம் எவன்கொல் செய்ததே', which is develops, not a shared image.
links.text_issue: Both verses flagged uncertain in sense

links.reason: 1265 answers the vow of 1261 only by sequence: the verse has the lord telling them 'நும்பெயர் நிறுத்துமின்', not explicitly sending them to fight or granting permission.
Both say what is not fated to one cannot be held: Kural 376 'பரியினும் ஆகாவாம்', PN-style proverb 'படற்பாலார் கண்ணே படுமே'. The palmyra and the night watchman make the abstract guarding concrete.

289 names only the dwellers of hell and the verse's last line blames the deed's wrath (மூழ்ந்தவினை முனியும்); TM 199 has Yama's messengers. 'How little each needs a judge' is an argument from silence, not a qualification.

Kings roaring for the girl (படாமுலைப் போகம் வேண்டி) matches the மகட்பாற் காஞ்சி situation. But the contest and her choice are not in the verse, and the epic assigns no blame to anyone or to a schemer; the poet's reassigning of blame is the grader's reading.

3030 compares plucking hair to a lion shedding its mane (துறப்பது); it states no impermanence and no king's wealth. The reason from Naladiyar 53 (நிலையாமை கண்டு துறப்பர்) is not in this verse, so the note reads it in.

539 'பான்மை' is the destined portion read by the astrologer; 554 'பாற்படு காலம் வந்தால் பான்மையார் விலக்குகிற்பார்' makes the king rest on it to refuse suitors. The prophecy visibly drives a decision. 'cast at birth' is not in the verse.
495 names only விஞ்சையன், and being Maruci is inferred; 427 praises his speech 'சொல்ல வல்லனே'. A bow on arrival hardly shows fitness for speech; this is sequence with a thin moral.

2260 offers 'விண்காவலை மகிழ்வீர்'; 2265 'விசும்பு அடைந்தான்' with celestial women worshipping: the offered heaven is delivered to the one who answers. Details of the duel are uncertain but the offer-and-fulfilment holds.
986 says the winner of the bride 'செய்தவம் உடைய காளை'; 1117 has the groom say 'தீண்டுதற்கு நோற்றேனே', taking up the very claim in a lover's mouth. The shift from release to desire is true.

Kural 221 defines giving by the need of the receiver; the poet is a poor bard (இரும்பேர் ஒக்கல் பெரும்புலம்பு) and the gift is a killer elephant he cannot use. The poem is a praise by complaint; it does not say it is not ஈகை, so 'would hardly count' is the note's overreach.

Sil 196 'ஆயிரத்து எட்டு நாமம்' and 204-205 'மலரடி ... தலைமிசை' set against CC 2 'ஆயிரத்து எட்டு மறு' and 'அடித்தாமரை சென்னி வைப்பாம்'. Names versus marks and the shared head-gesture are true; the note reads both correctly.

Both verses agree gods die; there is no incompatible claim in 2810 (gods blink, garlands wither) and TM 12 (many gods died). The 'cure' contrast is not in either Tamil text, and a Jain epic gains no Lord from a Saiva verse.

182 says even 'முழுதுணர்ந்த கடவுள்' is hard to truly know; TM 32 says 'தன்மை தானறிவார் இல்லை'. The Saiva verse does not deny all naming (line 4 is a song of grace) so 'denies any measure' overreads; the pair is a loose agreement.
Both name அருந்ததி for chastity, but the stock comparison carries no argument; 327 is also a ruse spoken to deceive. 'Equal versus surpasses' is a trivial difference, not a lesson about the star.
The queen's anger is real, but 1608 does not say the king praised a footprint or that he pleads; Kural 1313 is a sulk on a pretext. The note builds a qualification on narrative not in this verse.

'நாண் என்னும் கன்னிச் சிறை விண்டு' and Kural 1134 'நாணொடு நல்லாண்மை' both have love overcoming shame. But 1111 is blessing-free narrative, and the wedding is context outside the verse; 'blessed' is not stated.

Joining Ilanthiraiyan to Ilanthiraiyan relies on the colophon names alone; nothing in the Tamil of either fixes that the patron and the poet are the same. 'What praise did for a king who wrote about failure' is speculation.

Soolamani 5 excuses the poet's fault as the moon's spot; Naladiyar 221 advises keeping a friend's faults within, as rice has a husk. The rule is for friends, not readers, so 'a rule of reading' stretches the verse.

1859 compares death to a morsel in an elephant's mouth within a blink; Kural 334 makes the day a saw. Both say life is short, but the blade image is not in 1859, so 'the blink gains the blade' is not true.

3118's woman is the liberated state 'பிரிதலும் பிணியும் மூப்பும்' with no old age; Naladiyar 14 shows a bent woman 'தண்டுன்றா'. The contrast is thematic; the verse's 'இன்றேன்' looks corrupt and the Jain promise 'to those who give up' is not in the quatrain.
Siddhar 15 'தன்னுயிர்போல் எண்ணி' is a wish about lives; Yasodhara 197 has the eaten goat recognising the king 'என்மகன்'. The epic literalises the wish: the victim is kin. Both gains clauses are true.

1167 gives ஊழ்வினை as the cause of captivity and release; PN 192 'தீதும் நன்றும் பிறர்தர வாரா' is a similar stance. The rescuer-as-own-deed reading depends on 1172 and 943-948, not in this verse; the epic does not 'explain' the helper.
509 urges 'நகுக' in trouble; 582 'நாடகம் ... நக்கார்' is a different laugh after rescue. The 'staged' reading is the companions' figure of speech; sequence plus a thin link.

1470 and 1471 are adjacent verses in story order; neither states that the queen's fall causes the others' (each falls 'கண்டே'). 1470 is also a faint or death, uncertain. This is sequence, not development.

657 has birds falling 'மெய்ம் மறந்து வீழ்ந்தவே' and 659 has them flying 'அசிப்பபோன்று'. The contrast is real, but there is no conflicting claim, so tension does not fit; 659 reverses 657 and is better called develops.

2338 names no fault of the women and no cause for their tears; the Kural's tears are those of the oppressed. The 'wealth worn away by the city's tears' is not in the verse, so the pairing rests on the note's gloss.

Both paint a likeness on cloth (கிழிமிசை ... தீட்டி / தீட்டினான் கிழிமிசை), a real echo. But the nurse's verse shows the cousin's devotion only; Gunamalai's refusal is not in 1047, so the lesson rests on the plot outside it.

TM 149 'மன்றத்தே ... முக்கோடி வழங்கினான்' and 2984's funeral both concern the end of wealth, but joining them as 'before and after' is thematic. 2984 states the claim; TM 149 does not say mansion or palanquin were all public vanity.
300 'படையினது அமைதி கூழின் பகுதி' does echo army and food (Kural 381 படை, கூழ்). But the verse does not name lineage or learning, and its line 4 is obscure; 'counts as kingly worth' is read in.

Kural 146 already has அச்சம் (fear), so 'the verse adds fear and the Kural adds blame' is wrong; 2871 gives only 'வாள்போல் ... துன்பம்'. The parallel is real (another's wife brings suffering) but the teaching misreads the Kural.

Kural 85 asks whether the hospitable host's field needs sowing; PN 333 has the wife pounding 'குரல் உணங்கு விதைத்தினை' seed millet for guests. The poem shows the cost the rhetorical question passes over.
2197 'புலியாப் புறுத்திக் கொண்டேன்' and 2206 'சிங்கம் ... வேழத்தின் உயிர் விழுங்கும்' carry one beast figure, the sky-voice confirming his dread.

118 has the king carry the sword (வாள் கை ஏந்தி); 123 'கரத்து வாளும் ... விலக்கி நின்றோர் தெளிந்துணர்வு' has him check himself with the sword in hand, reversing his purpose. The point about means in hand is true.

161 compares the wealth of the guna-less to kongu 'கமழ மாட்டா'; Kural 1008 compares unloved wealth to a poison tree. Different qualities (no scent versus poison; 'worthless' versus 'unwanted'), and the 'harsher/softer' gains clauses are confused.

2093 'உற்றநாள் சிலநுமக்கு' is a king's address; Kural 342 is elliptical (வேண்டின் உண்டாகத் துறக்க) and its 'renounce while there is time' is an interpretive gloss. 'Ruler and father' is not in the couplet; the pairing is thin.

2337 has warriors ordering the women out; it does not say the king is dead, and Naladiyar 3 'வினை உலப்ப ... மாற்றார் கொள' has foes taking wives. The 'victors expel rather than take' contrast is the note's own, and Naladiyar does not claim taking is the only end.

1381 'விதிபடு மனிசரை வெருவி மீண்டனர்' and Kural 380 'ஊழிற் பெருவலி யாவுள' both make fate strongest. The verse illustrates the couplet without a condition added, so qualifies fits poorly; 'without any scheme named' is the note's claim.
1326 asks 'மங்கைகொல் ... பாவைகொல் ... இயக்கிகொல்'; 1327 answers with 'மாலை வாடின, வாட்கண் இமைத்தன, கால் பூமியைத் தோய்ந்தன' and names her. The later verse resolves the earlier doubt.

353 strips ornaments 'அகற்றிய' yet wishes 'உரவோன் சிறுவன் உயர்க'; Kural 341 'யாதனின் யாதனின் நீங்கியான் நோதல் அதனின் அதனின் இலன்'. The couplet's piecemeal logic reads the unrenounced tie as where pain stays; the later grief verses are cited in the marker's notes.

1807 has Vijayai lamenting; 1883 has Civakan weeping on hearing of her. The reciprocal tears are real, but the 'two halves of one grief' is sequence with a moral; the verses do not otherwise answer one another.

71 'மலமலி குரம்பை' (body a hut of filth) and Naladiyar 46's list of parts both teach the body's foulness. But 'a shared root with the mercy that stays the king's sword' is not in either text; the king's check at 123 is a different matter.
